title: afraegle gabonensis
intro: Afraegle gabonensis, commonly known as Gabonese Ironwood, is a plant species belonging to the Rutaceae family. It has been traditionally used in West African medicine for its potential health benefits, including its ability to treat fever, digestive issues, and skin infections. The bioactive constituents of Afraegle gabonensis include limonoids, flavonoids, and other compounds that are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The plant's therapeutic actions are thought to be mediated by its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce inflammation, and scavenge free radicals, making it a subject of interest for further research into its potential health benefits.
